name: The Bleed Flash
description: A spontaneous mass event triggered when enough BCIs in a given radius hit the same emotional frequency simultaneously — grief, rage, or euphoria — causing hundreds to stop moving and begin humming the same unplanned tone. No organizer has ever been identified. The events last between 90 seconds and four minutes, after which participants report feeling 'scraped clean.' The longest recorded Bleed Flash occurred at the Kessler-Wulandari Transit Hub in 2219, lasting eleven minutes and drawing over 2,400 participants, three of whom entered catatonic fugue states.
cultural_impact: Bleed Flashes have become informal grief rituals in neighborhoods with high casualty rates, appearing reliably in the days after mass Shelf violence or corporate evictions. Corponation Halversen-Okeke's neuro-monitoring division has spent Φ 4.2 million attempting to identify a trigger mechanism without success.
key_figures: Tessara Mbeki-Johansdóttir (neurologist, first academic to document the phenomenon)
The Hollow Choir (anonymous collective claiming spiritual authorship)
story_hooks: A Bleed Flash triggers in the middle of a corporate negotiation floor in Tier 4, implicating someone in the room of leaking emotional-frequency data to an unknown party.
A journalist investigating the Hollow Choir's claims discovers the flashes correlate precisely with unmarked deaths in Halversen-Okeke detention facilities.
A player character wakes up having lost four minutes — the exact duration of a Bleed Flash they have no memory of participating in, but their BCI logs show they were at the center of it.
